h1: The Bed Hotel 101 Roi Et — A Spacious City Hotel With Big Parking, a Short Walk to Bueng Phlan Chai
intro: If you're driving into Roi Et and want an in-town place with roomy, clean rooms and easy parking, The Bed Hotel 101 (Thebedhotel101) is a name guest reviews keep mentioning for its spacious, good-value rooms · It's a 3-star hotel on Rop Mueang Road in Mueang district, about a 10–12 minute walk to Bueng Phlan Chai and Roi Et Tower (101 Tower), near the King Rama VI Monument · There are 79 rooms from Superior up to Deluxe and Suite, breakfast included and large free parking, from approx. ฿790/night · Real guest reviews agree the rooms are spacious and clean, the beds comfortable, staff helpful, and it's central yet fairly quiet — though there are a few things to be aware of.

body.html: The Bed Hotel 101 is a 3-star, 79-room hotel in central Roi Et, set on Rop Mueang Road in Mueang district · It opened back in 2010 and had a major renovation in 2019, so while the building isn't brand new, the rooms have been refreshed · What puts this name on Roi Et's in-town shortlist is spacious, clean rooms and a big, easy car park · Room types run from Superior and Deluxe up to a Suite, suiting solo travellers, couples and small families who arrive by car.

Guests consistently praise the larger-than-expected rooms, soft comfortable beds, clean bathrooms and helpful, attentive staff · Every room has air-conditioning, a fridge, TV, hot-water shower, a tea/coffee maker and free Wi-Fi, and many look out over the city · There's an on-site restaurant and lounge with a small bar that several reviewers note has cheap drinks, a 24-hour front desk, and laundry service · Breakfast is included, which for a few-hundred-baht room in the city centre makes it feel genuinely well-equipped.
"Spacious, clean room with a comfortable bed. Central but quite quiet, walkable to Bueng Phlan Chai and the tower, and the parking is big and easy. Staff were helpful — great value for the price."

The location is another strong point · The hotel sits on Rop Mueang Road in central Roi Et, about a 10–12 minute walk to Bueng Phlan Chai (Somdet Park) and Roi Et Tower, near the King Rama VI Monument · Because it's on a ring road rather than the busy main drag, it's quieter than hotels right on the highway, yet still close to markets, restaurants and convenience stores · There's large free parking, ideal for self-drivers or anyone breaking up an Isan road trip.

To be straight, going by real reviews: the recurring notes are that some facilities fall a little short of expectations — water pressure can be weak in a few rooms, and some rooms have a slightly musty smell when you first open the door · The building opened in 2010, and even after the 2019 renovation a few things show their age · Breakfast is a small set with limited choice, so many guests head into town instead · And as a small hotel in a small city, the lift and service can be slow at busy times.

In short, if you want an in-town Roi Et hotel with spacious, clean rooms, easy parking, a short walk to Bueng Phlan Chai and the tower, breakfast included, and you don't mind that the building isn't brand new — The Bed Hotel 101 is a sensible pick · A score of 7.4 from 14 Trip.com reviews captures it well: good location, spacious clean rooms, good value, with minor caveats around water pressure, the odd musty room, and the building's age · It suits visitors here for Bueng Phlan Chai, the tower, temple-hopping, or a one-night stop on an Isan self-drive trip.

A tip from following the reviews here: at check-in, ask for a higher floor — the city views are nicer and it's usually quieter · Turn on the air-con and test the water as soon as you get in; if a room smells musty, open the window or ask to switch · And for breakfast, if you want more variety, head out to a morning eatery or coffee shop near Bueng Phlan Chai for a proper local Roi Et start to the day.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Bed Hotel 101 Roi Et

faq.q: Where is The Bed Hotel 101 in Roi Et, and what's nearby?
faq.a: The Bed Hotel 101 is at 52 Rop Mueang Road, Nai Mueang, in central Roi Et · It's about a 10–12 minute walk to Bueng Phlan Chai and Roi Et Tower (the city viewpoint), near the King Rama VI Monument · It sits on a ring road off the main highway, so it's fairly quiet while still close to markets, restaurants and convenience stores.

faq.q: How much does The Bed Hotel 101 cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from approx. ฿790/night for a Superior Room · Higher-floor Deluxe Twin and Deluxe Double rooms with city views run around ฿1,100–฿1,200 · The Suite, with a separate living room, is around ฿3,200 · Rates vary by room type and season, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does The Bed Hotel 101 have parking? Is it good for self-drivers?
faq.a: Yes · The hotel has large, easy free parking, a point guests often praise, making it ideal for self-drivers or a stop on an Isan road trip · It's central on Rop Mueang Road but off the main highway, so it's easy to get in and out and stays fairly quiet.

faq.q: Does The Bed Hotel 101 include breakfast?
faq.a: Yes, breakfast is included, served as a small set with fairly limited choice · Many guests head out to a morning eatery or coffee shop near Bueng Phlan Chai for more variety · Check at booking whether your rate includes breakfast.

faq.q: Are the rooms really spacious and good value?
faq.a: Most reviews confirm the rooms are larger than expected, clean, with soft comfortable beds and good value for a city-centre stay · Worth knowing: the building opened in 2010 (renovated 2019), so some fittings show their age, water pressure can be weak in places, and a few rooms smell musty on first opening — so check the room condition on arrival.

faq.q: Who is The Bed Hotel 101 best for?
faq.a: It's best for self-drivers visiting Roi Et who want an in-town hotel with spacious, clean rooms, easy parking, and a short walk to Bueng Phlan Chai and the tower · It suits solo travellers, couples and small families alike, and works well for anyone here for Bueng Phlan Chai, the tower, temple-hopping, or a one-night Isan road-trip stop.
